sections.subtitle: Telling Time - Hours
sections.content:
🕐 Basic Hour Format

1:00 is singular:
• Es la una → It's 1 o'clock

All other hours are plural:
• Son las dos → It's 2 o'clock
• Son las cinco → It's 5 o'clock
• Son las diez → It's 10 o'clock

⏰ Time of day:
• de la mañana → AM (morning)
• de la tarde → PM (afternoon)
• de la noche → PM (evening/night)

sections.subtitle: Telling Time - Minutes
sections.content:
⏱️ Adding Minutes

Minutes PAST the hour (use 'y'):
• Son las tres y diez → 3:10
• Son las cuatro y veinte → 4:20

Special terms:
• cuarto → quarter (15 min)
  → Son las dos y cuarto (2:15)
• media → half (30 min)
  → Son las cinco y media (5:30)

Minutes TO the hour (use 'menos'):
• Son las seis menos diez → 5:50
  (literally: 6 minus 10)
• Son las ocho menos cuarto → 7:45
  (literally: 8 minus quarter)

sections.subtitle: Parts of the Day
sections.content:
🌅 Time Periods

• mañana → morning
• mediodía → noon/midday
• tarde → afternoon/evening
• noche → night
• medianoche → midnight
• madrugada → early morning/dawn

📍 Using with 'por':
• por la mañana → in the morning
• por la tarde → in the afternoon
• por la noche → at night

sections.subtitle: Days & Months
sections.content:
📅 Days of the Week

• lunes → Monday
• martes → Tuesday
• miércoles → Wednesday
• jueves → Thursday
• viernes → Friday
• sábado → Saturday
• domingo → Sunday

📆 Months of the Year

• enero → January
• febrero → February
• marzo → March
• abril → April
• mayo → May
• junio → June
• julio → July
• agosto → August
• septiembre → September
• octubre → October
• noviembre → November
• diciembre → December

⚠️ NOT capitalized in Spanish
(unless starting a sentence)

sections.subtitle: Seasons & Dates
sections.content:
🌸 Four Seasons

• primavera → spring
• verano → summer
• otoño → fall/autumn
• invierno → winter

📍 Date Format

Pattern: el + number + de + month

Examples:
• el 15 de marzo → March 15th
• el 20 de julio → July 20th
• el 3 de octubre → October 3rd

⚠️ Special case for 1st:
• el primero de enero → January 1st
(not "el uno de enero")

sections.subtitle: Duration & Frequency
sections.content:
⏳ Time Expressions

Hace + time = ago:
• Hace dos días → two days ago
• Hace una semana → a week ago

Desde = since/from:
• Desde ayer → since yesterday
• Desde las dos → since 2 o'clock

Durante = during/for:
• Durante tres horas → for three hours
• Durante el verano → during the summer

🔄 Frequency Adverbs

• siempre → always
• nunca → never
• a veces → sometimes
• frecuentemente → frequently
• raramente → rarely

questions.question: How do you say 'It's 1 o'clock' in Spanish?
questions.hint: 1 o'clock is singular, so use 'Es la...' not 'Son las...'

questions.question: How do you say 'It's 3 o'clock' in Spanish?
questions.hint: All hours except 1 use 'Son las...' because they're plural.

questions.question: How do you say '2:15' (two fifteen) in Spanish?
questions.hint: In Spanish, 15 minutes is called 'cuarto' (quarter). Use 'y' to add minutes.

questions.question: How do you say '5:30' in Spanish?
questions.hint: 30 minutes is 'media' (half). It's 5 o'clock plus half.

questions.question: How do you express '6:50' (ten minutes to seven)?
questions.hint: For minutes to the hour, use 'menos' (minus). Think '7 minus 10 minutes'.

questions.question: What does 'de la mañana' mean?
questions.hint: 'Mañana' means morning when used with 'la'. It helps specify AM times.

questions.question: What is 'midnight' in Spanish?
questions.hint: It's one word combining 'media' (half/middle) and 'noche' (night).

questions.question: What is 'noon' or 'midday' in Spanish?
questions.hint: It combines 'media' (middle) and 'día' (day).

questions.question: What is Monday in Spanish?
questions.hint: Days of the week in Spanish are not capitalized. This one comes from 'Luna' (moon).

questions.question: What is Friday in Spanish?
questions.hint: This day is named after Venus. In Spanish, it ends in '-es'.

questions.question: Which month is 'enero'?
questions.hint: This is the first month of the year. It looks similar to English but starts with 'e'.

questions.question: What is 'August' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Named after the Roman emperor Augustus. In Spanish, it's written with lowercase unless starting a sentence.

questions.question: How do you say 'March 15th' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Format: el + number + de + month. Literally 'the 15 of March'.

questions.question: How do you say 'January 1st' in Spanish?
questions.hint: For the first day of any month, use 'primero' instead of 'uno'.

questions.question: What is 'summer' in Spanish?
questions.hint: This season comes from Latin 'veranum tempus'. It's the warmest season.

questions.question: What is 'winter' in Spanish?
questions.hint: This is the coldest season. Starts with 'inv-'.

questions.question: How do you say 'two days ago' in Spanish?
questions.hint: Use 'hace' + time period to express 'ago'. Hace literally means 'it makes'.

questions.question: What does 'desde ayer' mean?
questions.hint: 'Desde' means 'since' or 'from'. Ayer means 'yesterday'.

questions.question: What word means 'always' in Spanish?
questions.hint: This adverb means 100% of the time, every time, without exception.

questions.question: What does 'a veces' mean?
questions.hint: Literally means 'at times'. It indicates occasional frequency, not always or never.
